newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel Railways hit by wildcat strike.
newsitem.headline: Israel Railways hit by wildcat strike.

text.p: Workers at state-owned Israel Railway went on a 24-hour wildcat strike on Sunday to protest at a government plan to restructure the railway which they fear is a prelude to privatisation, a spokesman for the workers said.
"The prime minister made a decision without consulting us," Shaul Okish, a representative of the 1,300 railway employees, told Reuters in explanation for the strike call.

Israel Railway spokesman Beni Naor confirmed a decision had been made to break up the railways into separate infrastructure and operating companies but said there had been no decision on privatisation.
The strike halted the railway's 100 passenger and 200 freight trains.
To take up the slack, the national bus cooperative Egged added extra buses, mostly between Tel Aviv and the northern port city of Haifa. About 25,000 passengers use the trains daily.
"We're talking about a wildcat strike that is completely illegal and unnecessary," Amos Ozni, Israel Railways director-general, said in a statement.

The statement said the decision to split the concern into two was made "to significantly expand the operations of the railway throughout the country". Ozni said the workers had been informed of the decision last week.

"The director-general of the railway calls on the workers to return to work and to continue discussions with railway management on implementing the government decision," it said, adding that workers' rights would be protected.
The railroad, part of the Ports and Railways Authority, is in the process of a major expansion.
In October, Israel's transport minister went to New York in search of foreign investors for a package of infrastructure projects estimated at about $20 billion, including the railways.
The minister said at the time the government had not decided how to integrate private sector investment into the projects.
